Let

\[
f(x)=\lfloor 2x\rfloor+\lfloor 4x\rfloor+\lfloor 6x\rfloor+\lfloor 8x\rfloor.
\]

Set \(y=2x\). Since \(x\) ranges over all real numbers, so does \(y\), and

\[
f(x)=\lfloor y\rfloor+\lfloor 2y\rfloor+\lfloor 3y\rfloor+\lfloor 4y\rfloor.
\]

Write \(y=m+t\), where \(m\in\mathbb Z\) and \(0\le t<1\). Then for each positive integer \(k\),

\[
\lfloor ky\rfloor=\lfloor k(m+t)\rfloor=km+\lfloor kt\rfloor.
\]

Therefore

\[
f(x)=10m+\left(\lfloor t\rfloor+\lfloor 2t\rfloor+\lfloor 3t\rfloor+\lfloor 4t\rfloor\right).
\]

Since \(0\le t<1\), we have \(\lfloor t\rfloor=0\). Now compute the remaining expression according to the intervals of \(t\):

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
t\text{-interval} & \lfloor 2t\rfloor+\lfloor 3t\rfloor+\lfloor 4t\rfloor \\ \hline
[0,\frac14) & 0\\
[\frac14,\frac13) & 1\\
[\frac13,\frac12) & 2\\
[\frac12,\frac23) & 4\\
[\frac23,\frac34) & 5\\
[\frac34,1) & 6
\end{array}
\]

Thus every value of \(f(x)\) has the form

\[
10m+r
\]

where

\[
r\in\{0,1,2,4,5,6\}.
\]

Conversely, each of these six residues modulo \(10\) actually occurs, as shown by the table. Hence a positive integer is expressible exactly when its residue modulo \(10\) is one of

\[
0,1,2,4,5,6.
\]

Among the first \(1000\) positive integers, each residue class modulo \(10\) occurs exactly \(100\) times. Since there are \(5\) allowable residue classes, the number of expressible integers is

\[
5\cdot 100=500.
\]

\[
\boxed{500}
\]
